purpose: Record a located Abuan Watershed household resource-use source without turning source-reported river products into verified fish species occurrences.

waterbodyContext.identityLimit: The abstract explicitly attributes river products to Bintacan River but gives no catch station, coordinates, feature ID, or respondent-to-site crosswalk. Do not use this as river geometry or a precise capture locality.

studyAsReported.methodSummary: The abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods survey with interviews, focus-group discussions, and questionnaires administered to 379 household residents. It does not give a fish-collection design or identify a fish sampling period.
studyAsReported.sourceAccess: The article landing-page abstract was reviewed. The underlying article pages and any supporting data were not obtained in this review.

interpretationLimits: These are labels transcribed from the article abstract, not scientific identifications or an audited species checklist.
The source does not define local labels such as ikan, amlid, burasi, or karpa; do not translate or normalize them into taxa without the full article and qualified local/taxonomic review.
Tilapia is not resolved to a scientific species, and the report provides no voucher, specimen identifier, photograph, count, date of capture, or capture site.

The abstract describes household resource use, not standardized ichthyofaunal sampling; it cannot establish abundance, present-day presence, ecological diet, legal catchability, or a site-specific occurrence.
The source says river products from Bintacan River; it does not assign each listed label to an exact locality or distinguish all forms of collection and sourcing.

reuse.pageStatement: The journal landing page displays a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license.
reuse.disposition: Cite and link to the source; only concise labels and limitations are summarized for internal research. Do not copy article text, figures, or data files into Bangwit without a separate rights and source-quality review.

followUp: Obtain and review the complete article, including its sampling period, respondent locations, local-term definitions, and references.
Search for a separate fish survey, municipal fisheries inventory, or specimen-backed study for Bintacan/Abuan; keep household reports separate from biological occurrence records.
If local names remain important, request interpretation from Isabela State University, City of Ilagan ENRO, or BFAR Region II with the article citation in hand.

source.citation: Bacquel, J. M., & Ramos, A. M. (2020). Socio-economic characterization and resource use patterns of communities in the Abuan Watershed. International Journal of Psychosocial Rehabilitation, 24(8), 3403–3410. https://doi.org/10.61841/adpsgt07
source.supports: The abstract reports a 379-household watershed resource-use survey and lists tilapia, shrimps, ikan, udang, amlid, burasi, and karpa as river products from Bintacan River; it does not establish scientific identities or exact fish capture sites.
